column1: 09 -- Per-County / Per-Municipality Dataset Catalog (v10, CSV authoritative; Hamilton A01-A27 write 2026-10-17)
Purpose

Exhaustive per-jurisdiction dataset catalog: relevance review, 4-axis taxonomy, sensitivity review (and its access-tier correction, D-13), and -- this revision -- a correction to how source URLs were recorded.
NEW: catalogue_url column, and a project-wide fix to public_url

Earlier passes stored a Hub/CKAN/Socrata LANDING PAGE (a human-browsable webpage) in public_url for every dataset pulled by the exhaustive catalog script -- format literally read 'Web Page' on ~1,700 rows. That is not a download path. Checked the underlying cached DCAT/CKAN feeds directly and found they already carry the real machine endpoint (an 'ArcGIS GeoServices REST API' distribution, or a direct GeoJSON/CSV download URL) alongside the landing page -- the first extraction pass just used the wrong one.

Fixed 2026-09-23: 1,262 rows corrected across Hamilton, Niagara Falls ON, Welland, Brant County, Norfolk County, Brantford, Genesee County, Rochester (DCAT sources), Niagara Region/Fort Erie/Lincoln/NOTL/St. Catharines (CKAN), and Buffalo (Socrata, using the standard SODA `/resource/{id}.json` pattern). Haldimand County's 222 rows (resolved via ArcGIS Enterprise Portal item search, same landing-page problem) were fixed the same way once their item metadata was queried directly for each dataset's real service `url`.
- **public_url**: the actual download/query endpoint -- a FeatureServer/MapServer REST URL where available, else the best direct-download format found (GeoJSON > CSV > ZIP/Shapefile > KML).

- **catalogue_url**: the human-browsable listing/landing page (Hub dataset page, CKAN dataset page, Socrata `/d/` page, or an ArcGIS Portal item page) -- kept because it's often more informative for a person deciding whether to use a dataset, even though it's not what a script should hit.

51 rows have no non-webpage distribution at all (confirmed, not a gap) -- these are Hub web apps/experiences/StoryMaps with no underlying exportable data, correctly left with only a catalogue_url and no public_url.

This fix covers every jurisdiction pulled via the exhaustive DCAT/CKAN/Socrata/Portal-search scripts. It does NOT cover the small number of hand-curated rows built directly from a resolved service URL in the first place (Hamilton's original curated set, all NYS county parcel rows, Monroe County's NA-19 additions, etc.) -- those were already correct.
Everything below this point is unchanged from the prior README revision (v6).
sensitivity_flag policy correction (D-13)

sensitivity_flag means 'needs an access-tier decision' (see niagara-atlas/TECHNOLOGY-DECISIONS.md D-13), never 'delete this field.' Owner-of-record on several parcel datasets is often already public record in its source jurisdiction; the open question is presentation tiering, not deletion.
PART A -- project-relevance columns: review_status (admitted_in_mcs | curated_relevant | reviewed_relevant | reviewed_context | reviewed_not_relevant | reviewed_unclear), relevance_match.

PART B -- project-agnostic taxonomy: domain_primary (16-value vocabulary), domain_tags, domain_confidence, granularity (parcel_or_property | building_or_structure | point_facility | linear_network | area_or_zone | jurisdiction_aggregate | entity_or_person_level | unspecified), temporal_nature, sensitivity_flag (none | vulnerable_population_data | individual_health_or_social_data | property_ownership_pii | employee_hr_data | named_individual_data | protected_class_business_data), suggested_use_case.

Relationship to the other files: 07 answers 'does a portal exist for this jurisdiction', 08 hand-assesses parcel/contextual datasets and tracks sourcing alternatives, 02 (the MCS) is the master record of admitted datasets and this file is a provable superset of it. Access-tier/masking architecture decisions live in niagara-atlas/TECHNOLOGY-DECISIONS.md (D-13 onward).

Linear: NA-10 (parent), NA-18 (Brantford/Brant/Norfolk field verification, done), NA-19 (Monroe County folder drill-down, done), NA-20 (backlog: PII field audit on remaining parcel sources, manual review of unclear rows, sourcing decisions, MCS promotion, join-method taxonomy).
Built: 2026-09-23. Seventh revision the same day.

v8 update, 2026-09-25 (NA-21 full completion): the 4 sources flagged as 'still honestly incomplete' after the first NA-21 pass (Grand River CA, Hamilton CA, Brock University enumeration; NYS Open Data broad search; USGS National Map's other products; StatCan's dated editions; USDA's live replacement) were all dug into properly. Grand River CA (49 layers) and Hamilton CA (32 datasets) enumerated via their real ArcGIS servers/Hub feeds. Brock's 12 titles given individual rows. USDA Soil Data Access confirmed live via direct SQL query, one row per US county (94-268 map units each) with drainage-class/hydric-rating fields. StatCan's two Canadian Business Counts series (with/without employees) confirmed live with real CSV endpoints, full 2018-2026 date range. USGS National Map's Structures, Transportation, and GNIS products added. NYS Open Data's full 1,635-dataset catalog pulled and classified (152+51 relevant, 192+66 context, 225+472 not-relevant, 1059->470 unclear after one refinement round) -- the catalog is enormous and spans all of NY state government (lottery, MTA, professional licensing, corrections, etc.), so a meaningfully higher not-relevant/unclear ratio than the municipal pulls is expected and correct, not a sign of a weaker pass. Cross-Cutting Regional sheet: 39 -> 1,765 rows. Catalog grand total: 3,760 rows.

v9 update, 2026-09-25: systematic second sweep for un-enumerated multi-layer services. Checked all 290 rows whose public_url pointed at a bare MapServer/FeatureServer root rather than a numbered layer (live batch query of each). Found 31 genuine multi-layer services; exploded the 29 with real distinct content into 100 individual-layer rows (Monroe Census service revealed 3 poverty/equity layers -- HUD Low Income Population, ACS Poverty Stats, R/ECAPs -- previously invisible; Transportation revealed Alternative Fuel Stations; Monuments revealed GLONASS GPS base stations; Municipal_Assets/Sweden turned out to be a genuinely uncaptured town, not a duplicate of the 90-layer sewer service; NYS Building Footprints and USGS NHD split into their real layers). Confirmed 2 as true aliases of already-logged data (Municipal_Assets/Municipal_Assets = same data as DES/Municipal_Sewer_Systems; DOT/Service_Transportation = subset of Transportation/Transportation) -- noted, not duplicated. One 198-layer basemap (Base_Map/Monroe_Basemap_911) deliberately NOT exploded -- flagged as a scoping decision, not silently incomplete. 16 services now return Token Required where they previously (or presumably) did not -- flagged individually rather than assumed still-public. Catalog total: 3,949 -> 4,020 rows.
